text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Decathlete Erik Nool and cyclist Erika Salumae were voted best athletes of the year 1996.
- Russian State Duma vice-chairman Sergei Baburin made statements during his visit, which can be qualified as interference with Estonia's internal affairs, the foreign ministry said.
- The government is to decide today on cut-price train and bus tickets for students and the organisation of their use.
- The defence forces school for non-commissioned officers opened a new shooting range on December 21 with a contest for the army and police units of the Voru county.

- The daily interviewed David Peterson, president of American NRG Energy corporation, which signed a cooperation agreement with the Estonian government on Friday on the development and privatisation of Estonian power generating system.
- Swedish Sparbanken will buy 12.5 percent of shares of the Estonian Savings Bank from Hansapank. The latter will control less than five percent of Savings Bank.
- The government intends to establish an equal excise on central heating fuel and diesel fuel to avoid the use of the former by car owners. Heating fuel was so far exempt from the excise.
